q1_issues.issue: The "up to two years" bound is attached as a duration of the facing event, but the sentence measures the prison term the physician faces, not how long the facing lasts.
The object NP is "up to two years in prison", yet the Theme is the bare class `prison`, so the quantity that heads the object is severed from it and "in" is dropped.

q2_gaps: A modal-scoped indefinite subject carrying a restrictive relative clause ("a physician who performed the procedure could face …"): the indefinite-witness rule forces the relative clause to be asserted as a real past event, and no rule form is available (a verbal generic needs a bare plural or an explicit quantifier), so the hypothetical is recorded as fact.
"could" is absent from the modal sense-map (must -> Must/Obligated, may -> Might/Permitted, can -> Can/Permitted), so nothing fixes whether "could face" is epistemic, capability or deontic.

A duration-denoting object NP ("up to two years in prison"): the Measure/MeasureAtMost machinery attaches a bounded quantity to an entity, and no pattern mints a term/period entity for a bounded quantity that is itself the verb's object.
notes: `(Under sk_face_1 sk_legislation_1)` is the licensed framing-PP oblique (the "under maritime law" case) with the preposition actually used, and `(Might …)` correctly carries confidence 0.9 with no tense beside it.
